claim: Promoter islands are ~1 kbps (kilo base pairs) long.
source: Promoter islands are ~1 kbps (kilo base pairs) long (Bykov et al., 2020; Panyukov and Ozoline, 2013; Purtov et al., 2014; Shavkunov et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Each parent sequence contains on average ~5.32 –10 boxes and ~7.04 –35 boxes.
source: On average, each parent sequence contains ~5.32–10 boxes and ~7.04–35 boxes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 18 of the –10 boxes include the TGn motif upstream of the hexamer.
source: 18 of these –10 boxes also include the TGn motif upstream of the hexamer.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the parent sequences in the study.

claim: The mutagenesis library comprised 245,639 unique daughter sequences.
source: Our library comprised 245,639 unique daughter sequences, with an average of 4'913 daughter sequences per template and ~2.5-point mutations per daughter (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The mean coverage of possible mutational neighbors was 93%.
source: The mean coverage was 93% (minimum: 80%; maximum: 100%; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: 10 out of 50 parent sequences encode promoter activity before mutagenesis.
source: Because some sequences in our library are unmutated parent sequences, we determined that 10/50 of the parent sequences already encode promoter activity before mutagenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements of fluorescence from unmutated parent sequences.

claim: Three parent sequences drove expression on the top strand (P19-GFP, P20-GFP, P22-GFP).
source: Specifically, three parents drove expression on the top strand (P19-GFP, P20-GFP, P22-GFP), and seven did on the bottom strand (P6-RFP, P12-RFP, P13-RFP, P18-RFP, P19-RFP, P20-RFP, P21-RFP).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence measurements.

claim: Seven parent sequences drove expression on the bottom strand (P6-RFP, P12-RFP, P13-RFP, P18-RFP, P19-RFP, P20-RFP, P21-RFP).
source: Specifically, three parents drove expression on the top strand (P19-GFP, P20-GFP, P22-GFP), and seven did on the bottom strand (P6-RFP, P12-RFP, P13-RFP, P18-RFP, P19-RFP, P20-RFP, P21-RFP).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence measurements.

claim: Two parents harbor bidirectional promoters (P19 and P20).
source: Two parents harbor bidirectional promoters (P19 and P20).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence measurements showing expression from both strands.

claim: The remaining 40 parent sequences are non-promoters, with an average fluorescence score of 1.39 a.u.
source: The remaining 40 parent sequences are non-promoters, with an average fluorescence score of 1.39 a.u.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence measurements.

claim: 30% (15/50) of parents have the TGn motif upstream of a –10 box.
source: We also note that 30% (15/50) of parents have the TGn motif upstream of a –10 box, but only 20% (3/15) of these parents have promoter activity
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of parent sequences.

claim: Only 20% (3/15) of parents with the TGn motif upstream of a –10 box have promoter activity.
source: We also note that 30% (15/50) of parents have the TGn motif upstream of a –10 box, but only 20% (3/15) of these parents have promoter activity
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence measurements combined with computational motif analysis.

claim: The median Pnew for non-promoter parents is 0.046 (std. ±0.078).
source: The median Pnew is 0.046 (std. ±0.078), meaning that ~4.6% of all mutants have promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: The lowest Pnew is 0.002 (P25-GFP) and the highest 0.41 (P8-RFP), a 205-fold difference.
source: The lowest Pnew is 0.002 (P25-GFP) and the highest 0.41 (P8-RFP), a 205-fold difference.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: The inflection point of the fitted sigmoid curve relating Pnew to parent fluorescence is at 1.51 a.u.
source: The fact that the inflection point of the fitted curve is at 1.51 a.u. further justifies our use of 1.5 a.u. as a cutoff for promoter and non-promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on curve fitting to experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Pnew does not significantly correlate with the number of daughter sequences (p=0.529).
source: We found that Pnew does not significantly correlate with any of these features, including the number of –10 or –35 boxes (least squares linear regression, p=0.529, 0.930, 0.515, 0.652, respectively; Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (linear regression) of experimental data.

claim: Pnew does not significantly correlate with GC-content (p=0.930).
source: We found that Pnew does not significantly correlate with any of these features, including the number of –10 or –35 boxes (least squares linear regression, p=0.529, 0.930, 0.515, 0.652, respectively; Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (linear regression) of experimental data.

claim: Pnew does not significantly correlate with –10 box counts (p=0.515).
source: We found that Pnew does not significantly correlate with any of these features, including the number of –10 or –35 boxes (least squares linear regression, p=0.529, 0.930, 0.515, 0.652, respectively; Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (linear regression) of experimental data.

claim: Pnew does not significantly correlate with –35 box counts (p=0.652).
source: We found that Pnew does not significantly correlate with any of these features, including the number of –10 or –35 boxes (least squares linear regression, p=0.529, 0.930, 0.515, 0.652, respectively; Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 5A, B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (linear regression) of experimental data.

claim: Six k-mers (CTTC, GTTG, ACTTC, GTTGA, AACTTC, TAACTT) correlate with Pnew.
source: This analysis revealed six k-mers: CTTC, GTTG, ACTTC, GTTGA, AACTTC, TAACTT which correlate with Pnew.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (linear regression with multiple testing correction) of experimental data.

claim: The correlations between k-mers and Pnew are heavily influenced by an outlying Pnew value of 0.41 (P8-RFP).
source: However, these correlations are heavily influenced by an outlying Pnew value of 0.41 (P8-RFP; Figure 1—figure supplement 5C–H), and upon removing P8-RFP from the analysis, no k-mer significantly correlates with Pnew (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis showing that removing one data point eliminates the significance of the correlations.

claim: A total of 68 hotspots were identified across all 50 parent sequences.
source: Across all 50 parent sequences, we identified a total of 68 hotspots (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is based on mutual information analysis of experimental data.

claim: 34 hotspots occur in parent sequences with promoter activity.
source: 34 hotspots occur in the parent sequences with promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on mutual information analysis of experimental data.

claim: ~15% (5/34) of hotspots in promoter parents overlap exclusively with –10 boxes.
source: ~15% (5/34) of these hotspots overlap exclusively with –10 boxes, ~32% (11/34) with –35 boxes, and ~18% (6/34) overlap with both –10 and –35 boxes.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~32% (11/34) of hotspots in promoter parents overlap with –35 boxes.
source: ~15% (5/34) of these hotspots overlap exclusively with –10 boxes, ~32% (11/34) with –35 boxes, and ~18% (6/34) overlap with both –10 and –35 boxes.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~18% (6/34) of hotspots in promoter parents overlap with both –10 and –35 boxes.
source: ~15% (5/34) of these hotspots overlap exclusively with –10 boxes, ~32% (11/34) with –35 boxes, and ~18% (6/34) overlap with both –10 and –35 boxes.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~35% (12/34) of hotspots in promoter parents overlap with neither a –10 nor a –35 box.
source: The remaining ~35% of hotspots overlap with neither a –10 nor a –35 box (12/34).
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: Hotspots in biological parent sequences overlap significantly more with –10 and –35 boxes than scrambled parent sequences (chi-squared test, χ2=46.1, p=5.34 × 10–10).
source: Hotspots in the biological parent sequences overlap to a significantly greater extent with the two classes of boxes than the scrambled parent sequences (chi-squared test, 3 degrees of freedom, χ2=46.1, p=5.34 × 10–10).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical comparison (chi-squared test) between biological and scrambled sequences.

claim: 34 hotspots occur in non-promoter parent sequences.
source: The remaining 34 hotspots occur in non-promoter parent sequences.
evidence: The claim is based on mutual information analysis of experimental data.

claim: ~26% (9/34) of hotspots in non-promoter parents overlap with –10 boxes.
source: Of these 34 hotspots, ~26% (9/34) overlap with –10 boxes, ~26% (9/34) with –35 boxes, ~15% with both –10 and –35 boxes (5/34), and ~32% with neither motif (11/34) (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~26% (9/34) of hotspots in non-promoter parents overlap with –35 boxes.
source: Of these 34 hotspots, ~26% (9/34) overlap with –10 boxes, ~26% (9/34) with –35 boxes, ~15% with both –10 and –35 boxes (5/34), and ~32% with neither motif (11/34) (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~15% (5/34) of hotspots in non-promoter parents overlap with both –10 and –35 boxes.
source: Of these 34 hotspots, ~26% (9/34) overlap with –10 boxes, ~26% (9/34) with –35 boxes, ~15% with both –10 and –35 boxes (5/34), and ~32% with neither motif (11/34) (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: ~32% (11/34) of hotspots in non-promoter parents overlap with neither a –10 nor –35 box.
source: Of these 34 hotspots, ~26% (9/34) overlap with –10 boxes, ~26% (9/34) with –35 boxes, ~15% with both –10 and –35 boxes (5/34), and ~32% with neither motif (11/34) (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of hotspot locations relative to predicted motifs.

claim: Hotspots in non-promoter biological sequences overlap significantly more with –10 and –35 boxes than scrambled sequences (chi-squared test, χ2=21.4, p=8.75 × 10–5).
source: Again, these percentages of overlap with existing boxes are significantly greater for biological than for scrambled parent sequences (chi-squared test, 3 degrees of freedom, χ2=21.4, p=8.75 × 10–5).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical comparison (chi-squared test) between biological and scrambled sequences.

claim: There is no significant difference between the motif overlap of promoters and non-promoters (chi-squared test, χ2=2.51, p=0.473).
source: There is no significant difference between the motif overlap of promoters and non-promoters (chi-squared test, 3 degrees of freedom, χ2=2.51, p=0.473).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical comparison (chi-squared test) between promoter and non-promoter sequences.

claim: Only ~14% (37/266) of –10 boxes overlap within ±3 bp from a hotspot.
source: Of the 266 –10 boxes, only 37 (~14%) overlap within ±3 bp from a hotspot.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motif locations relative to hotspots.

claim: Only ~12% (43/352) of –35 boxes overlap with a hotspot.
source: Similarly, of the 352 –35 boxes, only 43 (~12%) overlap with a hotspot.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motif locations relative to hotspots.

claim: Only ~13% of all –10 and –35 boxes in the parents contribute to promoter activity.
source: Only ~13% of all –10 and –35 boxes contribute to de-novo promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of which motifs overlap with hotspots that affect fluorescence.

claim: On average, 39.5 and 39.4 new –10 and –35 boxes emerged at unique positions within the daughter sequences of each mutagenized parent.
source: On average, 39.5 and 39.4 new –10 and –35 boxes emerged at unique positions within the daughter sequences of each mutagenized parent (Figure 3A and B), with 1'562 and 1'576 new locations for –10 boxes and –35 boxes, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motifs in daughter sequences.

claim: 1,562 new locations for –10 boxes and 1,576 new locations for –35 boxes were created across all daughter sequences.
source: On average, 39.5 and 39.4 new –10 and –35 boxes emerged at unique positions within the daughter sequences of each mutagenized parent (Figure 3A and B), with 1'562 and 1'576 new locations for –10 boxes and –35 boxes, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motifs in daughter sequences.

claim: ~22% (684/3138) of new boxes are spaced 15–20 bp away from their cognate box.
source: ~22% (684/3138) of these new boxes are spaced 15–20 bp away from their cognate box, and ~7.3% (114/1562) of the new –10 boxes have the TGn motif upstream of them.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motif spacing in daughter sequences.

claim: ~7.3% (114/1562) of the new –10 boxes have the TGn motif upstream of them.
source: ~22% (684/3138) of these new boxes are spaced 15–20 bp away from their cognate box, and ~7.3% (114/1562) of the new –10 boxes have the TGn motif upstream of them.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motifs in daughter sequences.

claim: Only five of the new –10 boxes and four of the new –35 boxes are significantly associated with increasing fluorescence by more than +0.5 a.u.
source: However, only a mere five of the new –10 boxes and four of the new –35 boxes are significantly associated with increasing fluorescence by more than +0.5 a.u. (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis (Mann-Whitney U test) of fluorescence changes associated with motif gains.

claim: Only ~0.3% of all new –10 and –35 boxes actually create new promoter activity.
source: That is, only ~0.3% of all new –10 and –35 boxes actually create new promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on the ratio of boxes that significantly increase fluorescence to the total number of new boxes created.

claim: Parent P16-RFP gains promoter activity when mutations create a –10 box 17 bp downstream of a preexisting –35 box, increasing median fluorescence by +1.99 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=7.64 × 10–32).
source: Parent P16-RFP gains promoter activity when mutations create a –10 box 17 bp downstream of a preexisting –35 box (Figure 3E), increasing median fluorescence by +1.99 a.u. (Figure 3F; two-tailed MWU test, q=7.64 × 10–32).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: The majority of new –10 boxes in P16-RFP emerge when the sequence TAAACA (0.44 bits) mutates to TAAACt (7.28 bits).
source: The majority of these –10 boxes emerge when the sequence TAAACA (0.44 bits) mutates to TAAACt (7.28 bits).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of sequence changes in daughter sequences with new –10 boxes.

claim: A point mutation creating a –10 box in P16-RFP increases fluorescence ~11.2 fold compared to wild-type.
source: This experiment shows that fluorescence increases ~11.2 fold when the –10 box emerges (Figure 3F′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: Parent P1-RFP gains promoter activity when mutations create a –35 box 18 bp upstream of a preexisting –10 box, increasing fluorescence by +0.74 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=4.25 × 10–42).
source: Specifically, parent P1-RFP gains promoter activity when mutations create a –35 box 18 bp upstream of a preexisting –10 box (Figure 3G), which increases fluorescence by +0.74 a.u. (Figure 3H, two-tailed MWU test, q=4.25 × 10–42).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: The majority of new –35 boxes in P1-RFP emerge when the sequence ATGAGT (0.00 bits) mutates to tTGAGT (3.93 bits).
source: The majority of new –35 boxes emerge when the sequence ATGAGT (0.00 bits) mutates to tTGAGT (3.93 bits).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of sequence changes in daughter sequences with new –35 boxes.

claim: A point mutation creating a –35 box in P1-RFP shows a ~2.0-fold increase in fluorescence compared to wild-type.
source: A validation construct with this point mutation shows a ~2.0-fold increase in fluorescence compared to the wild-type (Figure 3H′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: Mutations do not create de novo promoter activity by destroying –10 and –35 boxes.
source: Mutations also destroy –10 and –35 boxes originally in the parent sequences, but this does not create de novo promoter activity (see Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of fluorescence changes when motifs are lost.

claim: 5 hotspots were identified in which losing a –10 box decreases expression in promoter parents.
source: We first identified 5 and 3 hotspots in which losing a –10 box or –35 box decreases expression (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when motifs are lost.

claim: 3 hotspots were identified in which losing a –35 box decreases expression in promoter parents.
source: We first identified 5 and 3 hotspots in which losing a –10 box or –35 box decreases expression (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when motifs are lost.

claim: For parent P12-RFP, losing a –35 box decreases fluorescence by –1.57 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=6.28 × 10–67).
source: For parent P12-RFP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), losing a –35 box decreases fluorescence by –1.57 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=6.28 × 10–67; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: For parent P12-RFP, losing a –10 box decreases fluorescence by –1.41 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=6.28 × 10–91).
source: and losing a –10 box decreases fluorescence by –1.41 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=6.28 × 10–91; Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: Scrambling the –35 box motif in P12-RFP lowers fluorescence by 62.6-fold.
source: Scrambling these motif sequences also lowers fluorescence by 62.6-fold and 49.7-fold respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D′, E′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: Scrambling the –10 box motif in P12-RFP lowers fluorescence by 49.7-fold.
source: Scrambling these motif sequences also lowers fluorescence by 62.6-fold and 49.7-fold respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D′, E′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: No hotspots were found in which destroying a –10 box or a –35 box increases expression by more than 0.5 a.u. in promoter parents.
source: We did not find any hotspots in which destroying a –10 box or a –35 box increases expression by more than 0.5 a.u. (see Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of fluorescence changes when motifs are lost in promoter parents.

claim: 329 new –10 boxes and 332 new –35 boxes are created at unique positions within daughter sequences of the 10 parents with promoter activity.
source: Our analysis found that across the 10 parents with promoter activity, 329 new –10 boxes and 332 new –35 boxes are created at unique positions within their daughter sequences.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of motifs in daughter sequences.

claim: Only 4 of the new –10 boxes further increase expression in promoter parents.
source: Despite this extensive gain of new boxes, only 4 of these new –10 boxes and 1 of these new –35 boxes further increases expression (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes associated with motif gains.

claim: Only 1 of the new –35 boxes further increases expression in promoter parents.
source: Despite this extensive gain of new boxes, only 4 of these new –10 boxes and 1 of these new –35 boxes further increases expression (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes associated with motif gains.

claim: For 4 new –10 boxes and 6 new –35 boxes, gaining the box decreases expression in promoter parents.
source: More surprisingly, for 4 and 6 of the new –10 and –35 boxes, gaining the box decreases expression (n=4 + 1+4 + 6, 15 hotspots with increased or decreased expression; Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes associated with motif gains.

claim: 6 of the 15 hotspots (40%) in promoter parents show homo-motif gains.
source: 6 of the 15 hotspots (40%) show homo-motif gains.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the types of motif overlaps in hotspots.

claim: 3 of the 15 hotspots (20%) in promoter parents show hetero-motif gains.
source: 3 of the 15 hotspots (20%) show hetero-motif gains.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the types of motif overlaps in hotspots.

claim: In P12-RFP, a point mutation creates a new –10 box that is +1 bp further from the –35 box and increases the PWM score of the original –10 box to match the consensus (TACAAT→TAtAAT), increasing median expression by +0.78 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=5.85 × 10–13).
source: For example in P12-RFP (Figure 4D), a point mutation creates both a new –10 box that is +1 bp further from the –35 box, but also increases the PWM score of the original –10 box to match the consensus (TACAAT→ TAtAAT). This point mutation increases median expression by +0.78 a.u. (Figure 4E); (two-tailed MWU test, q=5.85 × 10–13).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: A construct harboring the point mutation in P12-RFP that creates a homo-gain –10 box exhibits a 0.3-fold increase in fluorescence compared to wild-type.
source: A construct harboring this point mutation also exhibits a 0.3-fold increase in fluorescence compared to the wild-type (Figure 4E′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: For parent P22-GFP, mutations can change the –35 box into a –10 box, which decreases expression by –0.90 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=7.29 × 10–7).
source: For example, for parent P22-GFP, where our mutational data had allowed us to map the active –35 and –10 boxes (Figure 4F), mutations can change the –35 box into a –10 box, which decreases expression by –0.90 a.u. (Figure 4G; two-tailed MWU test, q=7.29 × 10–7).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental fluorescence data.

claim: A construct harboring the point mutation in P22-GFP that changes the –35 box into a –10 box exhibits a 13-fold decrease in fluorescence compared to wild-type.
source: A construct harboring this point mutation also exhibits a 13-fold decrease in fluorescence compared to the wild-type (Figure 4G′).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental validation using a plate reader.

claim: 4 of the 15 hotspots (~27%) in promoter parents are located in P20-GFP/RFP, which encodes a bidirectional promoter.
source: 4 of the 15 hotspots (~27%) are located in P20-GFP/RFP (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), which encodes a bidirectional promoter.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of hotspot locations and promoter activity.

claim: H-NS binds to ~5% of the E. coli genome.
source: H-NS binds to ~5% of the E. coli genome (Shimada et al., 2011), to horizontally transferred DNA (Navarre et al., 2007; Oshima et al., 2006), to transposons (Cooper et al., 2024), and to promoter islands (Purtov et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Six parent sequences were identified as H-NS target candidates (P2-GFP, P19-GFP, P20-GFP, P22-GFP, P12-RFP, and P20-RFP).
source: This approach identified six candidates for H-NS targets (P2-GFP, P19-GFP, P20-GFP, P22-GFP, P12-RFP, and P20-RFP).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of fluorescence in wild-type vs Δhns backgrounds.

claim: For GFP, the largest fluorescence change in the Δhns background occurs in P22-GFP, increasing fluorescence ~1.6-fold (two-tailed t-test, p=1.16 × 10–8).
source: For GFP, the largest change occurs in P22-GFP, increasing fluorescence ~1.6-fold in the mutant background (two-tailed t-test, p=1.16 × 10–8; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of fluorescence in wild-type vs Δhns backgrounds.

claim: For RFP, the largest fluorescence change in the Δhns background occurs in P12-RFP, increasing fluorescence ~0.5-fold (two-tailed t-test, p=4.33 × 10–10).
source: For RFP, the largest change occurs in P12-RFP, increasing fluorescence ~0.5-fold in the mutant background (two-tailed t-test, p=4.33 × 10–10; Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of fluorescence in wild-type vs Δhns backgrounds.

claim: For template P20, GFP expression increases ~2.6-fold in the Δhns background (two-tailed t-test, p=1.59 × 10–6).
source: We note that for template P20, which is a bidirectional promoter, GFP expression increases ~2.6-fold in the Δhns background (two-tailed t-test, p=1.59 × 10–6).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of fluorescence in wild-type vs Δhns backgrounds.

claim: For template P20, RFP expression decreases ~0.42-fold in the Δhns background (two-tailed t-test, p=4.77 × 10–4).
source: Simultaneously, RFP expression decreases ~0.42-fold in the Δhns background (two-tailed t-test, p=4.77 × 10–4; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of fluorescence in wild-type vs Δhns backgrounds.

claim: H-NS modulates the directionality of P20's bidirectional promoter through either cis- or trans-effects.
source: These findings suggest that H-NS also modulates the directionality of P20's bidirectional promoter through either cis- or trans-effects.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that H-NS affects GFP and RFP expression differently in P20.

claim: Two candidate H-NS motifs were identified in P12-RFP whose destruction is associated with fluorescence increases greater than 0.5 a.u.
source: This approach identified two candidate motifs in P12-RFP and one in P22-GFP whose destruction are associated with fluorescence increases greater than 0.5 a.u. (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when H-NS motifs are lost.

claim: One candidate H-NS motif was identified in P22-GFP whose destruction is associated with fluorescence increases greater than 0.5 a.u.
source: This approach identified two candidate motifs in P12-RFP and one in P22-GFP whose destruction are associated with fluorescence increases greater than 0.5 a.u. (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when H-NS motifs are lost.

claim: For P22-GFP, a H-NS motif lies 77 bp upstream of the mapped promoter, and mutations which destroy this motif significantly increase fluorescence by +0.52 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=1.07 × 10–3).
source: For P22-GFP, a H-NS motif lies 77 bp upstream of the mapped promoter. Mutations which destroy this motif significantly increase fluorescence by +0.52 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=1.07 × 10–3; Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when the H-NS motif is lost.

claim: For P12-RFP, one H-NS motif lies upstream of the mapped promoter's –35 box, and mutations that destroy this motif significantly increase fluorescence by +0.53 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=3.28 × 10–40).
source: For P12-RFP, one H-NS motif lies upstream of the mapped promoter's –35 box, and the other upstream of the mapped promoter's –10 box. Mutations that destroy these H-NS motifs significantly increase fluorescence by +0.53 and+0.51 a.u., respectively (two-tailed MWU test, q=3.28 × 10–40 and q=4.42 × 10–50; Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when the H-NS motif is lost.

claim: For P12-RFP, one H-NS motif lies upstream of the mapped promoter's –10 box, and mutations that destroy this motif significantly increase fluorescence by +0.51 a.u. (two-tailed MWU test, q=4.42 × 10–50).
source: For P12-RFP, one H-NS motif lies upstream of the mapped promoter's –35 box, and the other upstream of the mapped promoter's –10 box. Mutations that destroy these H-NS motifs significantly increase fluorescence by +0.53 and+0.51 a.u., respectively (two-tailed MWU test, q=3.28 × 10–40 and q=4.42 × 10–50; Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of fluorescence changes when the H-NS motif is lost.

claim: H-NS can suppress promoter emergence in certain contexts.
source: These findings ultimately demonstrate that H-NS can, in certain contexts, suppress promoter emergence (Forrest et al., 2022).

claim: The UP element plays a negligible role in promoter emergence within the dataset.
source: This finding ultimately suggests that the UP element plays a negligible role in promoter emergence within our dataset.

claim: Promoter emergence is best predicted by the level of background transcription each non-promoter parent produces.
source: Instead, we present evidence that promoter emergence is best predicted by the level of background transcription each non-promoter parent produces, a phenomenon also referred to as 'pervasive transcription' (Kapranov et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is based on the sigmoid relationship between parent fluorescence and Pnew, and is supported by a citation.

claim: Sequences that produce pervasive transcripts may have a proclivity for evolving de-novo promoters compared to other sequences.
source: From an evolutionary perspective, this would suggest that sequences that produce such pervasive transcripts – including the promoter islands (Panyukov and Ozoline, 2013) and the antisense strand of existing promoters (Dornenburg et al., 2010; Warman et al., 2021), may have a proclivity for evolving de-novo promoters compared to other sequences (Kapranov et al., 2007; Wade and Grainger, 2014).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the relationship between background transcription and Pnew, and is supported by citations.

claim: –10 and –35 boxes are not likely to repress promoter activity.
source: In sum, –10 and –35 boxes are not likely to repress promoter activity.
evidence: The claim is based on the lack of evidence for repression by these motifs in the experimental data.

claim: Mutations can readily create promoters with a wide dynamic range of activity.
source: These observations demonstrate how mutations can readily create promoters with a wide dynamic range of activity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that new motifs overlapping existing ones can increase or decrease expression.

claim: The ability to create promoters with a wide dynamic range facilitates natural selection's fine-tuning of a promoter to precise expression levels.
source: This ability facilitates natural selection's fine-tuning of a promoter to precise expression levels, within a small sequence search space that is easily accessible by few DNA mutations.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that mutations can modulate expression in various ways.

claim: True promoters in sequences enriched with promoter motifs typically overlap with multiple –10 and –35 boxes.
source: The finding also supports a previous conclusion that true promoters in sequences enriched with promoter motifs typically overlap with multiple –10 and –35 boxes (Huerta and Collado-Vides, 2003).
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that promoters are modulated when new motifs overlap existing ones, and is supported by a citation.

claim: We are still underestimating the complexity of promoters.
